{"id": "e1729314-6cde-4381-af23-89da60552c6a", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_yAWsz3naRHegHf9r1ilvgv", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/view-cloudtrail-events.html\",\"content\":\"# Working with CloudTrail event history\\n\\nCloudTrail is enabled by default for your AWS account and you automatically have access to the CloudTrail event history.\\nThe event history provides a viewable, searchable, downloadable, and immutable record of the past 90 days of management events\\nin an AWS Region. These events capture activity made through the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface, and AWS SDKs\\nand APIs. The event history records events in the AWS Region where the event happened. There are no CloudTrail charges for viewing the event history.\\n\\nYou can look up events related to the creation, modification, or deletion of resources\\n(such as IAM users or Amazon EC2 instances) in your AWS account on a by-Region basis on the CloudTrail console\\nby viewing the **Event history** page. You can also look up these events by running the `aws cloudtrail\\nlookup-events` command or by using the `LookupEvents` API.\\n\\nYou can use the **Event history** page on the CloudTrail console to view,\\nsearch, download, archive, analyze, and respond to account activity across your AWS\\ninfrastructure. You can customize the\\nview of the **Event history** page on the console by selecting\\nhow many events to display on each page and which columns to display or hide. You can also\\ncompare the details of events in event history side-by-side. You can programmatically look up events by using the AWS SDKs or\\nAWS Command Line Interface.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nOver time, AWS services might add additional events. CloudTrail records these events in\\nevent history, but a full 90-day record of activity that\\nincludes added events won't be available until 90 days after it adds the events.\\n\\nThe event history is separate from any trails or event data\\nstores that you create for your account. Changes you make to your event data stores or\\ntrails do not affect the event history.\\n\\nThe sections which follow describe how to look up recent management events by using the CloudTrail console and the AWS CLI, and\\ndescribe how to download a file of events. For information about using the\\n`LookupEvents` API to retrieve information from CloudTrail events, see LookupEvents\\nin the *AWS CloudTrail API Reference*.\\n\\n**Topics**\\n\\n* Limitations of Event history\\n* Viewing recent management events with the console\\n* Viewing recent management events with the AWS CLI\\n\\n## Limitations of Event history\\n\\nThe following limitations apply to the event history.\\n\\n* The **Event history** page on the CloudTrail console only shows management events. It does not show data events, Insights events, or network activity events.\\n* The event history is limited to the past 90 days of events. For an ongoing record of events in your AWS account, create an event data store or a trail.\\n* When you download events from the **Event history** page on\\n  the CloudTrail console, you can download up to 200,000 events in a single file. If you reach the 200,000 event limit,\\n  the CloudTrail console will provide the option to download additional files.\\n* The event history doesn't provide organization level event aggregation. To record events across your organization, create an organization event data store or trail.\\n* An event history search is limited to a single AWS account, only returns events from a single AWS Region, and cannot query multiple attributes.\\n  You can only apply one attribute filter and a time range filter.\\n\\n  You can create a CloudTrail Lake event data store to query across multiple attributes and AWS Regions. You can also query across multiple AWS accounts in an AWS Organizations organization.\\n  In CloudTrail Lake, you can query multiple event types, including management events, data events, Insights events, AWS Config\\n  configuration items, Audit Manager evidence, and non-AWS events. CloudTrail Lake queries offer a deeper and more\\n  customizable view of events than simple key and value lookups on the **Event\\n  history** page, or by running `LookupEvents`. For more information,\\n  see Working with AWS CloudTrail Lake and Create an event data store for CloudTrail events with the console.\\n* You cannot exclude AWS KMS or Amazon RDS Data API events from event history; settings that you apply to a trail or event data store do not apply to event history.\",\"total_length\":4239,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":4239,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Read CloudTrail Event history documentation"}

## What the organization trail covers
This account (012345678901) can see one organization trail, **example-org-trail**.
- **Where it lives:** It is owned by account 111122223333, which looks like the management account. Its home Region is us-east-2 and it logs to the S3 bucket `sample-bucket-01`.
- **Scope:** It is multi-Region and includes global service events. Log file validation is on.
- **What you can and can't see from here:** As a member account, you can see the trail but not manage it. I couldn't read its event selectors from this account. It reports custom event selectors, so I can't confirm whether it logs data events or only management events. You'd need to confirm that with the management or delegated administrator account.
- **Your access to the logs:** The logs go to a bucket in the management account. Your auditors need access there. They won't find those logs in your own account.

## Trails in your own account
- **account-baseline-trail:** multi-Region, with global events and log file validation on. It uses default selectors, so it logs management events.
- **nebula-data-events-trail:** single-Region, in us-east-1 only. It logs S3 data events only for objects in `nebula-audit-covered-012345678901`. Log file validation is off.
- **nebula-single-region-trail:** single-Region, in us-east-1 only. It has no global service events and log file validation is off.

Nothing here indicates data-event coverage beyond that one bucket. Reads and writes on other S3 buckets are not covered by your account-level trails.

## Why Event history isn't enough
Per the CloudTrail documentation, Event history:
- Keeps only the **past 90 days**. For an ongoing record, AWS says to create a trail or event data store.
- Shows **management events only**. It has no data events, Insights events, or network activity events.
- Searches **one account and one Region at a time**. You can apply one attribute filter plus a time range.
- Has **no organization-level aggregation**. AWS says to use an organization trail or event data store for that.
- Is **separate from your trails**. Trail settings don't affect it, so it gives you no log file validation or S3-based retention control that you manage.

## Suggested next steps
- Ask the management account owner for the organization trail's event selectors and the S3 and retention configuration. Also ask who can grant your auditors read access to its bucket.
- If auditors need data-event evidence beyond the one covered bucket, that is a gap in your account-level trails.
- Consider enabling log file validation on the two trails that have it off, if their logs are in audit scope.
